metadata.title: Velmont Logistics SA v. Orbis Retail Belgium NV
metadata.summary: Velmont Logistics seeks recovery of unpaid freight and warehousing invoices while Orbis Retail disputes service levels, detention charges, and contractual surcharges.
metadata.author: GENESIS

actors.name: Player
actors.description: Counsel responsible for the Velmont Logistics matter.

actors.name: Velmont Logistics SA
actors.description: Belgian freight and warehousing provider seeking payment.

actors.name: Orbis Retail Belgium NV
actors.description: Retail customer disputing charges and service quality.

actors.name: Velmont Operations Manager
actors.description: Operational witness for performance and detention records.

facts.statement: Velmont performed the invoiced freight and warehousing services.
Orbis has not paid the invoices identified in Velmont's ledger.
Velmont's logistics terms were incorporated into the parties' contract.
The detention and fuel surcharges have a contractual basis.
Velmont's alleged service failures caused loss that Orbis may set off.

evidence.title: Master services agreement and logistics terms
evidence.description: Executed framework agreement, tariff schedule, and incorporated terms.

evidence.title: Invoice and payment ledger
evidence.description: Reconciled invoices, credits, payments, and outstanding principal.

evidence.title: Proof-of-delivery bundle
evidence.description: Signed delivery records and warehouse movement confirmations.

evidence.title: Vehicle detention records
evidence.description: Time-stamped arrival, release, and waiting-time records.

evidence.title: Orbis service complaints
evidence.description: Contemporaneous complaints relied on for the proposed set-off.

actions.title: Audit the invoice and evidence file
actions.description: Reconcile principal, identify disputed surcharges, and test the proposed set-off against contemporaneous records.

actions.title: Issue a documented formal demand
actions.description: Send the reconciled demand with contractual terms, delivery proof, and a response deadline.

actions.title: Accept negotiated payment
actions.description: Resolve the disputed surcharges and set-off through an agreed payment and final settlement.

actions.title: Present the claim for judgment
actions.description: Proceed on the documentary record and answer the service-level and set-off defences.

actions.title: Complete judgment enforcement
actions.description: Provide the enforceable title, recover payment, and close the client matter.

outcomes.title: Negotiated recovery
outcomes.summary: Velmont accepts a documented payment resolving the invoice balance, disputed surcharges, and Orbis's proposed set-off.

outcomes.title: Judgment recovered and enforced
outcomes.summary: Velmont obtains and enforces judgment on the documented logistics debt after addressing the disputed service and surcharge issues.

metadata.title: GreenFire — The First 72 Hours
metadata.summary: An industrial fire places a chemical-storage company under simultaneous criminal, regulatory, environmental, insurance, and insolvency pressure. Preserve evidence, control communications, protect coverage, manage conflicts, and hand over a defensible crisis position within 72 hours.
metadata.author: GENESIS: AI Juris

actors.name: Player
actors.description: Crisis counsel responsible for the GreenFire matter.

actors.name: GreenFire Industrial Solutions B.V.
actors.description: Chemical-storage operator affected by the fire.

actors.name: Eva de Wit
actors.description: Managing director and primary client contact.

actors.name: Daan Vermeer
actors.description: Operations manager with knowledge of the affected storage site.

actors.name: Port Haven Environmental Authority
actors.description: Lead environmental regulator investigating the incident.

facts.statement: Hot work may have been performed near chemical storage shortly before the fire.
Chemical materials may have been stored outside the permitted zone.
An internal safety warning may not have been escalated to management.
The managing director may have lacked specific knowledge of the site practice that preceded the fire.
Potentially responsive insurance policies require prompt incident notice.

actions.title: Accept the emergency mandate
actions.description: Confirm representation and establish a privileged crisis channel.

actions.title: Issue an evidence-preservation hold
actions.description: Preserve logs, CCTV, manifests, emails, maintenance data, and incident communications.

actions.title: Assess company/director conflicts
actions.description: Assess whether corporate and personal interests permit joint representation.

actions.title: Appoint separate counsel for the director
actions.description: Protect privilege where personal and corporate interests may diverge.

actions.title: Notify all potentially responsive insurers
actions.description: Send controlled notice across all potentially responsive policies.

actions.title: Review the preliminary fire assessment
actions.description: Convert preliminary findings into a controlled legal risk map.

actions.title: Open a controlled regulator channel
actions.description: Separate urgent factual cooperation from unreviewed legal admissions.

actions.title: Submit the reviewed initial response
actions.description: Provide time-critical facts through the controlled channel while reserving legal positions.

actions.title: Release the requested files without review
actions.description: Send the shared-drive export immediately, risking uncontrolled disclosure.

actions.title: Establish the integrated crisis-response protocol
actions.description: Lock all crisis workstreams into one controlled protocol.

actions.title: Hand over a protected crisis position
actions.description: Deliver the handoff with evidence, coverage, representation, communications, and causation work controlled.

actions.title: Hand over a compromised crisis position
actions.description: Close the first 72 hours with material unresolved exposure.

inbox_items.subject: URGENT: Fire at the GreenFire storage site
inbox_items.body: A major fire has caused runoff, police attendance, regulatory inspection, and media attention.

inbox_items.subject: Evidence preservation must begin immediately
inbox_items.body: CCTV, logs, manifests, maintenance data, and communications are at risk.

inbox_items.subject: Coverage counsel: notice deadlines may apply
inbox_items.body: Late notice could create coverage and funding disputes.

inbox_items.subject: Potential conflict between GreenFire and its director
inbox_items.body: Early accounts of storage practices and operational instructions may diverge.

inbox_items.subject: Environmental authority demands records
inbox_items.body: The authority requests site plans, inventories, permits, inspections, and incident messages.

inbox_items.subject: Preliminary fire assessment is ready
inbox_items.body: The expert identified a probable ignition sequence and records requiring preservation.

inbox_items.subject: Partner requests the 72-hour crisis handoff
inbox_items.body: Summarise evidence, representation, coverage, communications, findings, deadlines, and next steps.

events.title: Preliminary assessment was not reviewed in time

outcomes.title: Protected crisis position
outcomes.summary: Evidence is preserved, conflicts controlled, insurers notified, communications reviewed, and causation risk assessed.

outcomes.title: Compromised crisis position
outcomes.summary: Material exposure remains in preservation, coverage, conflicts, expert review, or regulatory disclosure.

en.caption: Port Haven Environmental Authority v. GreenFire Industrial Solutions B.V.
en.synopsis: An industrial fire places GreenFire under simultaneous regulatory, environmental, insurance, criminal, and governance pressure. Crisis counsel must preserve evidence and hand over a defensible position within 72 hours.
legal_issues: evidence preservation after a major incident

ru.caption: Port Haven Environmental Authority v. GreenFire Industrial Solutions B.V.
ru.synopsis: Промышленный пожар создаёт для GreenFire одновременные регуляторные, экологические, страховые, уголовно-правовые и корпоративные риски. Кризисный юрист должен сохранить доказательства и передать защищённую позицию в течение 72 часов.
